# Yusen Logistics opens £280m Northampton distribution centre

- Business Times 
- October 5, 2026 

Yusen Logistics has officially opened its £280 million Northampton distribution centre at SEGRO Logistics Park Northampton, creating the company’s largest facility anywhere in the world.

The 1.2 million sq ft Sustainable Distribution Centre at Milton Malsor, close to Junction 15 of the M1, began operating in June before its official opening ceremony on September 24. Around 150 people are expected to work at the site.

SEGRO has put Yusen Logistics’ commitment to the Northampton distribution centre at £280 million. The logistics company was the first customer to take a building at the 600-acre SEGRO Logistics Park Northampton development.

David Evans managing director of Yusen Logistics UK Photo Yusen Logistics

results.author: Caroline Peachey

Thermotraffic opens automated cold store in Wrexham | Logistics Manager

# Thermotraffic opens automated cold store in Wrexham

By Caroline Peachey 6th October 2026 2 Mins Read

Temperature-controlled logistics provider Thermotraffic has expanded its distribution centre in Wrexham with a new automated cold store.

The expansion, completed on 28 September 2026 and operational from October, adds around 19,300 pallet spaces.

It takes total capacity at the site to around 33,150 pallet spaces, equivalent to 77,000 tonnes.

The development is Thermotraffic’s first automated warehouse in the UK. The company said the automated systems have been introduced to improve operational efficiency and workplace safety.

The expansion includes a new production area, bringing storage, handling and services, including labelling, repacking, X-ray and metal detection, blast freezing, up-tempering and microwaving, together at the Wrexham facility.

Thermotraffic said combining additional storage capacity with handling and production services at the same location is intended to help customers reduce unnecessary movements in supply chains and respond more effectively to seasonal peaks and changing volumes

Richardson Barberry has announced the practical completion of leading premium parcel delivery firm DPD’s new purpose-built distribution hub at Forrest Park, the £250 million business park development located at Newton Aycliffe, County Durham.

The 63,000 sq ft Grade A logistics facility has been delivered on behalf of DPD, which has committed to a 25-year lease on the eight-acre site. The new hub – located adjacent to Junction 59 of the A1(M) – has the potential to create up to 250 additional roles as DPD expands its operations in the North East.

### VB Distribution has opened its new business park in Lancashire, adding 100,000 sq. ft of bonded warehousing to its national network of depots

Marking the latest milestone in the group’s long-term expansion programme, the site cements VB Distribution’s position as the market leader ahead of the sector’s biggest regulatory shift in a decade.

The site expands the group’s HMRC-approved customs bonded warehouse operation, one of the few in the sector, allowing duty-suspended storage at a scale others cannot match. # Warehouse pioneers robotics system used in China

Image source, Kate Bradbrook/BBC

Image caption, Brian Luck says the Northampton warehouse is a "pioneering site" with its robotic system

By Kate Bradbrook, in Northampton and Louise Parry

27 September 2026

A new giant warehouse in England's logistics "golden triangle" is adopting pioneering technology previously only used in China, a company said.

Yusen Logistics UK said it will use a robotics and four-way conveyor system at its new site on the edge of Northampton, which will also employ hundreds of staff.

"There are some roles that robots can do better than people, but fundamentally robots don't work without people," said David Evans, the company's managing director.

The Japanese firm opened its 1.1m sq ft (102,193 sq m) site with a fusion ceremony that included a traditional counting song, sushi, and fish and chips.

Melba Swintex to open new 52,742 sq ft distribution facility in Rossendale - Made in Britain

 

 

 

 

 

Melba Swintex to announce the official opening of its new facility at Ewood Bridge, Rossendale, marking a significant investment in the company’s long-term growth, operational capacity and commitment to the region.

Founded in 1982 and built on decades of manufacturing heritage in Lancashire, Melba Swintex remains a proud third-generation family business. From early innovation in traffic cone manufacture through to the merger of Melba and Swintex in 2007, the company has continued to grow while staying true to its roots, combining technical expertise, craftsmanship and a long-term commitment to customers and community.

The new facility represents an important milestone for the business, which is one of the UK’s leading manufacturers of Temporary Traffic Management solutions and exports worldwide. Built to support increased demand and improve operational efficiency, the site will strengthen Melba Swintex’s ability to serve customers across the UK and internationally while supporting future expansion.
